title: Degree-zero normalization of abelian Čech comparisons
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\iota$ a type, $U_i$ a family of opens with $\sup_i U_i=X$, and $F$ an abelian sheaf [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Let $c:\check H^0(U,F)\to H^0(X,F)$ be an additive map satisfying IsAbelianCechComparison in degree zero [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction]. Then $c$ equals the inverse of the canonical restriction isomorphism $F(X)\to\check H^0(U,F)$ [lem-pc-topological-cech-zero-gluing-iso], followed by the inverse of the canonical Ext-zero-to-sections isomorphism. No comparison in another degree and no quasi-isomorphism hypothesis on $\alpha$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 20.11.2, construction of H(beta) H(alpha) inverse and independence of the resolution

proof.text: Fix an injective resolution I and a Čech zero class x. Use extMk_surjective to represent c(x) by an Ext-zero cocycle a. Evaluate its adjoint at 1 and lift the resulting section to a cycle z; the cocycle condition makes this possible, and iCycles monicity gives uniqueness. Apply the degree-zero comparison predicate to x, a and z.

Since there are no negative terms, homologyπ in degree zero is invertible for both source and total complexes. Lift the equality to zero cycles, apply iCycles and project to the (0,0) summand. The explicit alpha and beta formulas say that the section of a restricts to the resolution augmentation of the compatible family represented by x. Glue x using cechCohomologyZeroIso; separatedness of I-zero identifies that section with the augmentation of the glued section.

Exactness of the augmented injective resolution in degree zero factors a uniquely as b followed by I.ι.f 0, where b maps the constant integer sheaf to F. The Ext-zero cocycle formula identifies extMk(a) with Ext.mk₀ b, and functorHZeroIso evaluates b at 1. The restriction equality from the preceding step and monicity of I.ι.f 0 identify that section with the glued section. Cancel functorHZeroIso to obtain the desired equality on x, and conclude equality of additive morphisms by extensionality. The empty cover forces an empty space, where these groups are zero; the gluing theorem includes infinite covers.

from.place: Proof step 3: degree-zero normalization from the quotient equation

lean.statement:
theorem abelianCechComparison_zero_normalization
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    (c : (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyFunctor U 0).obj F ⟶
      (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) 0).obj F)
    (hc : IsAbelianCechComparison U F 0 c) :
    c = (TopCat.Sheaf.cechCohomologyZeroIso U hcover).inv.app F ≫
      (Sheaf.functorHZeroIso (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) isTerminalTop).inv.app F
